cards.question: Where should you apply defensive validation of user input?
cards.answer: Do not trust user input. Put validators on form values and on the HTTP request body and query.

cards.question: Should you validate responses from backend services your own team manages?
cards.answer: No. If you need to be defensive against your own teammates' code, you have gone too far. Those validators introduce too many edge cases.

cards.question: If the backend returns a string instead of an array, should the frontend fall back to []?
cards.answer: No. The frontend should not validate that and fall back to an empty array. The UI can show an error via an error boundary, or simply break, because invariants have broken.

cards.question: Should the UI refuse to break no matter what?
cards.answer: No. Push back on the attitude that the UI must never break. If invariants have broken, the UI can show an error using an error boundary or simply break.

cards.question: What happens if you treat the backend as an antagonist to your code?
cards.answer: You will soon start to see the backend developers as antagonists to you.
